(BY SMT.GIRIJA HIREMATH, HCGP FOR R1;
 SRI LINGESH KATTIMANI, ADVOCATE FOR R2)
 THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED U/S 483 OF BNSS,
 SEEKING TO GRANT THE BAIL IN FAVOUR OF THE  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:13126  CRL.P No. 102391 of 2024 PETITIONER/ACCUSED NO.1 HEREIN CONCERNED, IN SPL.SC.NO.41/2021 ON THE FILE OF 2ND ADDL. DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE, DHARWAD AND SPECIAL COURT FOR TRIAL OF THE OFFENCES UNDER THE POCSO ACT AND SC AND ST (POA) ACT FOR THE ALLEGING OFFENCE PUNISHABLE U/S 354(A) AND 376 OF IPC AND SECTION 6 AND 8 OF POCSO ACT.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
CORAM:

THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE V.SRISHANANDA  ORAL ORDER (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE V.SRISHANANDA) Heard Sri Raghavendra A. Purohit,
learned counsel for the petitioner/accused and Smt.Girija Hiremath, learned High Court Government Pleader.

2. Successive bail request of the petitioner in Special SC No.41/2021 on the file of the II Addl.
District and Sessions Judge, Dharwad.

entities.text:
II Addl.
District and Sessions Judge, Dharwad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Earlier bail request was rejected by this Court and according to the petitioner/accused, the changed circumstance is the examination of the victim, complainant and other material witnesses and continuation of the petitioner in judicial custody is thus no longer warranted as the Trial has progressed.
Per contra, Smt. Girija Hiremath, learned High Court Government Pleader, opposes the bail grounds by contending that the victim has supported the case of the prosecution in toto.

Admittedly,
victim being a minor and 'child' as defined under the Protection of Children against Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the theory of consent if any, loses its significance and having regard to the unequivocal testimony of the victim, this Court cannot entertain the successive bail request of the petitioner as there is no positive changed circumstance in the case of the petitioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having heard the parties, this Court perused the material on record, meticulously.

6. On such perusal of the material on record, especially the deposition of the victim which has been filed along with the bail request, it is crystal clear that, admittedly the victim girl is a minor and therefore, her consent, if any, is of no consequence.
7. Offence alleged against the petitioner is under Section 6 of the Protection of Children against Sexual Offences Act r/w Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Protection of Children against Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Taking note of the gravity of the offence and the theory of consent having lost its significance, this Court is of the considered opinion that the bail grounds urged in the bail petition are not sufficient enough to accede to the request of the petitioner for enlarging him on bail.

9. Ends of justice would be met with by directing the Trial Court to conclude the trial in a time bound manner as early as possible, taking note of the fact that accused is in judicial custody for about three years.

10. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER (i) Bail petition rejected.
(ii) Learned Trial Judge is directed to conclude the Trial as early as possible, not later than 30th November 2024.
